Senses.Explanation: An established senior Chan teacher: someone treated as worth consulting, able to receive students, or recognized among the leading elders of a region or earlier generation. The compound occurs 1,906 times in 291 allowlisted texts. Xiaoyao Cong's biography says he traveled south to consult such elders before meeting Huilin Zongben. Ying'an Tanhua praises the old senior teachers who bore their communities without weariness, and Tianru Weize says earlier senior teachers offered expedient instruction when students would not immediately take responsibility. Zhongfeng Mingben tells a student there are many old senior teachers in every region whom he may question. In Huangbo Xiyun's recorded exchange, an unnamed monk objects that established elders everywhere gather communities and teach people after Huangbo says there are no Chan teachers; Huangbo answers that he did not say there was no Chan, only that there were no teachers. Qianyan Yuanzhang uses 'one of this sort is called a venerable elder' satirically, showing that the social title can be quoted and mocked rather than simply bestowed. The term also supplies the document title Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters.
Senses.Note: The corpus provides no stable graph-formula definition of the bare title. The four strings ending in 'venerable elder is ...' are relative-clause constructions, not definitions. Productive modifiers include 'in every region' (71 hits in 55 texts), 'old' (22 in 19), and 'elder predecessors' (10 in eight).
